description: We are a team from Brazil interested in technology and space exploration. Our goal is to develop an interactive application using NASA data, combining creativity, clear information, and a user-friendly design. We want to learn, collaborate, and turn our idea into a working prototype.
summary:
Health7 is a functional prototype that supports preventive health monitoring for astronauts during space missions. It brings together physical measurements, cognitive assessments, behavioral check-ins, and personal health records to help crew members recognize changes and understand when to act.

The platform compares current records with each astronaut’s individual baseline and monitoring history. Explicit rules flag changes, while an AI assistant explains the findings and organizes a preventive follow-up plan, including when medical evaluation should be sought.

Health7 also includes reaction-time tests, NASA space-weather context, wearable connectivity options, a menstrual health calendar, and summaries for medical review.

Using NASA data and research resources, the project addresses the challenge of turning fragmented health information into clear next steps when immediate support from Earth may be limited.

Developed by Rulima Tech, the prototype demonstrates its monitoring workflow with synthetic crew scenarios. It supports preventive care and medical evaluation; it does not diagnose diseases or replace healthcare professionals.
details:
Health7 is a preventive health-monitoring prototype developed by Rulima Tech for astronauts during space missions.

THE PROBLEM

During long missions, health changes can develop while immediate medical support from Earth is limited. Physical measurements, cognitive assessments, symptoms, and behavioral records may be difficult to interpret when viewed separately. Astronauts need understandable information about what has changed and what to do next.

HOW IT WORKS

Health7 brings health records together and compares current measurements with each astronaut’s personal baseline and monitoring history.

The prototype uses explicit monitoring rules to flag changes. Its assistant explains selected findings in accessible language and helps organize preventive follow-up actions, including repeat measurements, continued observation, and seeking medical evaluation when appropriate.

Monitoring states are determined by the rule-based engine. The AI explanation layer does not independently determine those states or provide a medical diagnosis.

MAIN FEATURES

• Physical check-ups and comparisons with individual baselines.
• Cognitive assessments involving reaction time, memory, and attention.
• Behavioral check-ins and symptom records.
• NASA DONKI space-weather context.
• Wearable integration options, including compatible Bluetooth heart-rate sensors and health-data imports.
• A menstrual health calendar for recording dates, flow, pain, and symptoms.
• Preventive follow-up plans and summaries for medical review.

The menstrual calendar is optional and based on personal records. It does not assume a standard cycle or predict menstruation. Space-weather information provides mission context and is not interpreted as personal radiation dose.

CREATIVITY AND INTENDED IMPACT

Health7 connects personal health trends with clear explanations and practical next steps. Its proposed contribution is an understandable monitoring experience that helps astronauts act on changes rather than interpret disconnected measurements alone.

The intended impact is to support preventive care, reduce delays in recognizing relevant changes, and organize information for medical evaluation.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

The project uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js, Fastify, and PostgreSQL. Optional n8n workflows support the AI explanation layer. GSAP and JavaScript coordinate the landing-page demonstration.

NASA DATA AND RESEARCH

NASA resources inform the project’s mission context and design. These include DONKI space-weather information, Human Research Program risk references, and research on astronaut health monitoring and medical autonomy. Specific sources and their uses are listed in the NASA Data section.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS AND LIMITATIONS

The team considered individual baselines, clear explanations, traceable monitoring rules, communication interruptions, and the distinction between recorded data and simulated examples.

The demonstration uses synthetic crew scenarios and simulated sensor interactions. Available integration options should not be interpreted as validated continuous monitoring across all devices.

Health7 has not been clinically validated or deployed in spaceflight. It does not diagnose diseases, prescribe treatment, or replace healthcare professionals. NASA resource use does not imply NASA endorsement.

NEXT STEPS

Future work includes validation with medical specialists, testing with controlled user studies, improved sensor interoperability, stronger offline operation, and evaluation of mission-specific monitoring protocols.
